jurisdiction.name: Norway
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Norway follows its 2020 national AI strategy and is implementing the EU AI Act through the EEA: a draft AI Act (KI-loven) naming the communications authority Nkom as coordinating supervisor went to consultation in 2025, with a bill now aimed at spring 2027. A new Public Administration Act adopted in 2025 sets rules on automated decisions, explanations and documentation, and data protection law applies the GDPR. The Data Protection Authority runs a long-standing AI sandbox and publishes AI guidance, the Auditor General audited AI use in central government in 2024, and the health and education directorates have AI plans and advice.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digitalisation and Public Governance
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The government's main website blocked access, so the national AI strategy and the draft AI Act consultation could only be located, and several government documents are listed as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation (Kommunal- og moderniseringsdepartementet)
instruments.current_status: Norway's national AI strategy, presented 14 January 2020 by the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation (date per the government's press release 'Regjeringen legger frem nasjonal strategi for kunstig intelligens', which could not be opened). Riksrevisjonen's Dokument 3:18 (2023–2024) cites it as the current national strategy in 2024; digitalisation policy since 2024 sits with the Ministry of Digitalisation and Public Governance, whose 2024 national digitalisation strategy also covers AI (see leads). An official English version is published on regjeringen.no (id2685594, /en/).
instruments.summary: The 2020 national AI strategy sets out the conditions for developing and using AI in Norway: data and data management, language resources (Norwegian and Sami), AI-friendly regulation, education and skills, research and innovation, communication networks and computing capacity. It sets out seven ethical principles for responsible and trustworthy AI, based on the EU high-level expert group guidelines, and commits the government to measures including regulatory sandboxes (incl. the Datatilsynet AI sandbox). It is a non-binding policy document addressed to government and the public and private sectors.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; anchors ethics principles, the Datatilsynet sandbox and public-sector AI work.

instruments.official_title: Høring – utkast til ny lov om kunstig intelligens – gjennomføring av EUs forordning om kunstig intelligens i norsk rett
instruments.english_title: Consultation – draft new Act on artificial intelligence – implementation of the EU Artificial Intelligence Regulation in Norwegian law
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digitalisation and Public Governance (Digitaliserings- og forvaltningsdepartementet)
instruments.current_status: Sent on public consultation on 30 June 2025 (consultation deadline reportedly 30 September 2025); the law was planned to apply from late summer 2026, but as of 12 October 2026 no bill had been submitted to the Storting. A government press release of 4 August 2026 reportedly announces a new consultation in autumn 2026 because of EU amendments to the AI Act (simplification package), with the bill aimed at spring 2027, so the EU AI Act does not yet apply as Norwegian law.
instruments.summary: Draft AI Act (KI-loven) that would incorporate the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) into Norwegian law via the EEA Agreement and add supplementary national provisions. Per the government and regulators, Nkom is to be the national coordinating AI supervisory authority, with sector supervisors responsible in their areas, and the law establishes a regulatory sandbox for AI run with Digdir and Datatilsynet. The law is to apply alongside the Personal Data Act.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Norway's national implementation of the EU AI Act through the EEA; designates AI supervisory authorities.

instruments.english_title: Act on the processing of personal data (Personal Data Act)
instruments.issuing_authority: Storting; administered by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security
instruments.current_status: In force since 20 July 2018 (LOV-2018-06-15-38), as amended. Incorporates the GDPR into Norwegian law via the EEA Agreement.
instruments.summary: The Personal Data Act incorporates the GDPR into Norwegian law as part of the act, including Article 22 on automated individual decision-making and profiling, and adds national supplementary rules. It governs the processing of personal data for training and use of AI systems and is supervised by Datatilsynet. The draft AI Act is intended to apply alongside it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing AI training and use; basis for Datatilsynet AI guidance and sandbox.

instruments.current_status: Submitted to the Storting by the Auditor General on 2 September 2024.
instruments.summary: Performance audit presented to the Storting on the use of AI in central government agencies. It finds that agencies exploit AI unevenly and little, that legal clarification, infrastructure, data, skills and Norwegian language resources are lacking, that ethical principles for responsible AI are followed to varying degrees, and that coordination of public-sector AI is inadequate. It recommends that the Ministry of Digitalisation and Public Governance strengthen coordination and enablers, and includes the minister's reply.

instruments.english_title: Advice on artificial intelligence in schools
instruments.issuing_authority: Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training (Utdanningsdirektoratet)
instruments.publisher_name: Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training
instruments.current_status: Guidance page; the date is the "Sist endret" (last changed) date 2 December 2025, the only date stated. After the government's recommendation of 19 June 2026 that pupils in grades 1-7 should in principle not use generative AI, Udir is preparing new age-differentiated recommendations (page last changed 25 June 2026; see leads).
instruments.summary: National advice from Udir to school owners, school leaders, teachers and parents on the use of AI in schools. It sets out recommendations such as covering AI-related topics in the curriculum, letting teachers judge when AI is relevant, varying teaching and assessment, using only solutions approved and privacy-assessed by the school owner, and showing particular caution with younger children. Use of AI must rest on local legal, ethical and pedagogical assessments.

instruments.official_title: Lov om saksbehandlingen i offentlig forvaltning (forvaltningsloven)
instruments.english_title: Act on case handling in public administration (Public Administration Act)
instruments.issuing_authority: Storting (bill Prop. 79 L (2024–2025) from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security)
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Storting on 11 June 2025 (Lovvedtak 119 (2024–2025), Innst. 478 L, Prop. 79 L (2024–2025)); under § 99 it enters into force when the King decides and will repeal the Public Administration Act of 10 February 1967. No entry-into-force date was found; the sanctioned law's Lovdata number was not confirmed.
instruments.summary: The new Public Administration Act replaces the 1967 act and includes the first general rules on automated case handling in Norwegian public administration. § 11 allows agencies to automate case handling and decisions where the usual requirements are met, but not decisions covered by GDPR Article 22 without a specific legal basis; § 12 requires safeguards against errors and unfair discrimination and suitable statistical methods for Article 22 decisions and gives a right to an explanation and manual review; § 13 requires agencies to document and, as a rule, publish the legal content of automated case-handling systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated (algorithmic) decision-making and transparency of rules-as-code systems in the public sector.

Record the final recommendations once published.
